annotations.text:
Direction: stop styling the widget and start inheriting JupyterLab.

Every colour and font here is a --jp-* variable that JupyterLab already defines. That single decision fixes three of the four problems at once:

· dark mode works because the tokens change with the theme, not because we wrote a second stylesheet
· the Google Fonts @import disappears, so the widget stops breaking offline and stops phoning out
· it looks like part of the notebook instead of a navy rectangle pasted into one

The fourth (truncated buttons) is fixed by putting labels above fields instead of right-aligning them inline, which frees the whole row width for real button text.

Also changed:

· save/load glyphs were unicode characters that render as boxes in many fonts — now inline stroked SVG on a 24px grid
· the four ungrouped rows become four labelled sections, so the eye can find the resource fields without reading every label
· a header states which cluster you are about to run on, and whether it answered
· the output area is a real log surface rather than an unstyled ipywidgets Output
